data.gender_notes: Mawaadah is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic root 'w-d-d', meaning 'to promise' or 'to fulfill a promise'. In Islamic tradition, Mawaadah is a symbol of the eternal promise and covenant between Allah and His creation. The name Mawaadah carries the meaning “Promise, Covenant, Commitment” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Mawaadah usually hope their child will grow to embody promise, covenant, commitment and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.cultural_impact: The name Mawaadah holds a profound cultural impact in the Islamic world, serving as a reminder of the sacred covenant between Allah and His creatures. In various contexts, it signifies the importance of keeping promises and fulfilling one's duties towards the divine and others. For instance, during the Hajj pilgrimage, Mawaadah refers to the sacred promise purified souls make as they circle the Kaaba seven times, reaffirming their devotion to Allah and their commitment to upholding Islamic values.
data.spiritual_significance: On a deeper spiritual level, Mawaadah invokes the concept of du'a (supplication) and the belief in Allah's mercy and forgiveness. When one makes a sincere and heartfelt prayer to Allah, it is considered a fulfillment of a promise - a pledge to seek His love, guidance, and support. Through Mawaadah, we are reminded of the power of prayer and the importance of maintaining a close connection with Allah, as we strive to keep our promises to Him and to ourselves. Ultimately, it is a name that inspires hope, faith, and a deep reverence for the divine promise of salvation and eternal happiness.
